newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease further, rally seen April.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease further, rally seen April.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fell at the open on Thursday and dealers said the thin market could be stagnant through early April, when new quarterly allocations from institutional investors were expected to buoy the market.
"The market is extremely weak and there's a clear downward trend. At practically every level there's a lot of selling," said ING Baring's trader Vladislav Leonchuk.
Electric company UES EESR.RTS eased to $0.1840 at 1100 GMT from Wednesday's close of $0.1943. Shares of oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS ticked down to $13.87 from $13.98.
But Andrei Ippolitov, head of trading at Prospekt, said small investors and those new to the volatile Russian market were the primary sellers, and trade volumes have been low.
He said the small sellers were trying to stem losses made over the last couple of weeks, and which he said would be reversed in April for those who kept their positions.
Leonchuk said there was no positive news to lift prices.

"After shareholders meetings, lots of companies are announcing losses for the year. The new government still hasn't announced any global reforms and the US rate hike didn't exactly have a positive effect either," he said.
"Taking all that into account plus the market rally at the beginning of the year, I think there'll be room for profit-taking for some time to come."

Ippolitov said a new flow of funds from Western investors, the driving force behind the two month New Year rally which sent the RTS index soaring over 50 percent, was likely in April when new allocations were made by fund managers.
"I think everyone will have money next month," he said.
